question: Which of the following relief features is not an effect of internal forces of the Earth ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Residual Mountain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Residual Mountain**

 
 
• Mountain which is worn down due to a process of erosion for a long time by agents like wind, air, water.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/66b8e297bf2b4f168fe9c1ba477f30173daec824f5afc47e18347463d6586595.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Graben**

 
 
• Graben is a depressed block of the crust of a planet due to internal disturbances.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fa21b7681c0fcd24294ee6625fa65d9d57413b32262935c0c90b2c35de2a6c0e.png] 

 
• **Horst**

 
 
• A horst is a raised fault block bounded by normal faults.
 
• A horst is a raised block of the Earth's crust that has lifted or has remained stationary, while the land on either side (graben) has subsided.
 
 
 
• **Rift Valley**
 
 
• A rift valley is a linear-shaped lowland between several highlands or mountain ranges created by the action of a geologic rift or fault. A rift valley is formed on a divergent plate boundary, a crustal extension or spreading apart of the surface, which is subsequently further deepened by the forces of erosion.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/525c866024f9d500338f90c25875a26220411aa52662d6d7b03c60be6e087fc4.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Internal forces** of the earth result in earthquakes and volcanoes.
 
• The forces which originate from within the earth’s crust or inside the earth are called **internal or endogenetic forces**.
 
• The sources providing them energy are the internal heat, chemical reactions taking place within the earth.
